rationale: Slow-transit constipation rats received immature medicinal Citrus preparations, bran-fried material or constituents; not raw ripe orange or human Parkinson symptoms.
Herbal laxative review names Citrus sinensis and other plants, describes preclinical or traditional sources; source abstract does not establish human raw orange clinical constipation comparison.

Initial encounter records include constipation in 1,022 of 3,206 encounters. Mixed decoction prescriptions include zhi qiao, zhi shi and chen pi. The study measures prescription frequencies and baseline symptoms without a consumption measure or a change in constipation.

MEDI-PD randomized whole-diet counseling plus standard care versus standard care, 45 randomized and 36 analyzed; constipation changes p=.600 between arms, orange intake and its independent effect unspecified.
Review concerns iron regulation and PD gut pathogenesis, not an orange intervention or constipation estimate.
Review on gut-brain axis, microbiota, neurodegeneration and immune pathways; no human raw-orange constipation comparison in abstract.
PD gut-brain axis overview with microbiome-directed interventions; no orange exposure and symptom estimate in abstract.
MEDI-PD protocol NCT04683900; same study family as O05/1, planned dietary counseling and constipation endpoint, no individual orange comparison.
PD pharmacomicrobiomics review mentions Mediterranean diet and probiotics; no raw-orange clinical symptom estimate in abstract.
Review of PD microbiota and gut-brain treatment pathways, not an original isolated orange constipation comparison.
Review of gut dysbiosis and psychiatric disease in Alzheimer and Parkinson, no orange clinical bowel comparison in abstract.

Leão 2011 n12 chagasic megacolon, daily blended peeled orange with papaya, prunes and cream plus physiotherapy; within-patient symptom improvement without untreated control, no orange attribution; locally accessioned.
52 children randomized to PEG laxative formulas; commercial comparator is orange-grapefruit flavored PEG, not raw fruit or an isolated orange test.
US cross-sectional vegetable subtypes and constipation; orange is vegetable color category, not citrus fruit.
Huo preprint of same O04/4 fruit meta-analysis; orange juice and other fruits pooled, not a separate primary or raw-orange outcome estimate.

Published Huo 2022 systematic review; fruit and orange-juice findings aggregate heterogeneous trials. Authors explicitly distinguish juice from whole orange; underlying Lima 2019 juice study already catalogued.
ISRCTN12453166 protocol for a four-herb mixture including medicinal citrus peel for diarrhea-predominant IBS; not raw orange or measured constipation results.
Alexander crossover n91 orange juice plus 10 g pomace fiber versus juice alone; stool frequency interaction p=.46; both receive juice, not raw whole fruit, same prior accession.
Systematic review of mixed medicinal herbal formula including citrus peel for diarrhea-predominant IBS; not a raw-orange comparison.

Niv 2012 randomized levan versus control in 500 mL natural orange juice for eight weeks in 48 healthy adults. Both arms receive juice; uncontrolled pre-post stool increases cannot attribute a controlled effect to orange.
Purified naringin in experimentally induced rat colitis; diarrhea and stool measures are not raw orange or human constipation.
Healthy adults randomized dextrin versus maltodextrin mixed in orange juice; both receive juice and the test is fiber tolerability, not an orange contrast.
Post-ileal-pouch survey groups citrus fruit or juice, reports perceived looser stools and frequency; self-reported intolerance without orange-specific preparation or comparative PD outcome.
Ispaghula laxative product Fybogel Orange; orange is product flavor, not an isolated raw fruit test.
Infant iron supplement tolerability; some doses dissolved in orange juice, but adverse constipation not stratified by juice exposure; no orange effect.
After ileal pouch, orange juice carries acetaminophen for gastric emptying comparison by stool frequency; no assigned orange treatment effect.
Rat colitis imaging uses acridine orange fluorescent dye, not orange fruit exposure.
Constipation study compares ispaghula husk Fybogel Orange with other laxatives; orange is product name/flavor, not fruit treatment.
